title: Buttonhole stitch
subtitle: A close-packed looped edging for fabric and cutwork
excerpt: Buttonhole stitch works the same looped motion as blanket stitch but places each bar directly against the last, with no gap between them. The packed loops form a firm, dense edge that holds fabric from fraying and is the classic finish for cutwork and needle-made lace.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), buttonhole stitch entry. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), buttonhole stitch entry.

content.text: Buttonhole stitch and blanket stitch share one motion. The difference is spacing. Blanket stitch leaves a visible gap between each upright bar. Buttonhole stitch places bars directly beside each other, touching, so the looped base becomes a solid corded line. That firm edge resists fraying and is strong enough to use as a foundation for needle-made lace, as a cutwork finish, and as a tight decorative border.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 strands for a firm edge; 2 strands for fine cutwork

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Evenweave linen or cotton; felt for practice

items.label: Hoop
items.value: 15 cm hoop to keep fabric taut

content.text: Fasten the thread on the back of the fabric. Bring the needle up at point (A), on the inner line. This sets the height of every bar in the row.
Insert the needle down at point (B), directly on the outer edge and one thread-width to the right of (A). Bring the tip up at point (C), on the inner line directly above (B).
Before pulling through, pass the working thread under the needle tip from left to right, so it sits below the needle.
Pull the needle through and draw the thread down firmly. The loop locks at the outer edge as a small knot, forming one upright bar. The bar should sit flush against the previous one with no gap.
Repeat steps 2 to 4, placing each new (B) immediately beside the last bar. At the end of the row, take the thread down just past the final loop to hold the edge cord in place.

items.cause: Each new insertion point is placed too far from the previous one.
items.fix: Place point (B) of each stitch directly beside the last completed bar before pulling through.

items.symptom: The looped base line twists or looks uneven
items.cause: The thread is not fully under the needle tip before pulling, or tension varies between stitches.
items.fix: Check the thread lies cleanly under the needle before every pull, and keep tension consistent throughout the row.

items.cause: The needle is not entering the fabric at a right angle to the edge.
items.fix: Keep the needle perpendicular to the working line on every insertion.
